roadEnds: The foot of the Great Lift

cards.subject: A river canyon
lines: The spires are water-carved. Before the Sundering this was a gorge with a river running through it, and the sandstone needles are what the water left.
The Sundering pushed it above the water table. The eastern lake dried into salt flat and the gorge went to sand.

cards.subject: You are walking on the floor
cards.tag: In the modern game this is a lake
lines: Cataclysm collapsed the canyon walls and flooded the whole zone.
Every guide, screenshot or memory with boats in it, or a barge, or a whale shark, is a different place from this one.
Here it is sandstone and salt, edge to edge, and all of it is walkable.

cards.subject: Henrig Lonebrow
cards.tag: At the foot of the lift
lines: A dead dwarf with a weathered journal on him. It is not soulbound — you can post it to a friend.
Reading it sends you west to Thalanaar, and what he learned turns into the run on Charlga Razorflank in Razorfen Kraul.
He was in her cell block. He got out and died here anyway, carrying the message.

cards.subject: The zone has two floors
lines: Bridges have been built across the tops of the spires, joining pathways from mesa to mesa above the canyon.
It is designed to be walked at two heights, and in here both of them are dry.

cards.subject: The Galak
lines: This is Galak country — Splithoof Crag their village, Camp E'thok the outpost they hit caravans from.
Their founding khan was the fifth of Zaetar and Theradras' brood, and the Galak hold no alliance with their brother tribes.
The centaur here are the ones nobody else claims.

cards.subject: Freewind Post
lines: The tauren live on top of a mesa because they were driven up there — the Grimtotem below them, Galak war bands on the canyon floor and the flats.
They are living precariously on the tips of the high mesas.
It is the zone's only Horde flight point.

cards.subject: Highperch
lines: The western plateau is wyvern nesting ground, and in here they are hostile.
The zone's harpies are somewhere else entirely, at Roguefeather Den.
People get these two mixed up constantly.

cards.subject: Gornia
lines: There is a Thousand Needles subzone that never shipped. The wiki keeps its page purely for historical purposes.
From the name alone, the guess is that it was going to be an ogre settlement.
Galak Hold went the same way.

cards.subject: Weazel's Crater
lines: A large deep hole in the salt, full of saltstone basilisks.
Nobody knows who Weazel was. The name suggests either the man who found it or the man who made it.
The likeliest answer is that something the racers built landed here.

cards.subject: Rustmaul Dig Site
lines: The dwarves dug until they broke through into a subterranean silithid hive.
They were also driven out by a Horde raid under Moktar Krin.
One dig, two unrelated reasons to leave it.

cards.subject: The ship on the salt
lines: The Shimmering Flats are a dried lakebed, and the evidence is sitting on them: a wrecked sailing vessel.
A ship, hundreds of miles from any sea, on ground the goblins now drag-race across.

cards.subject: The Mirage Raceway
lines: Pozzik and Fizzle Brassbolts built the track to settle whether goblins or gnomes make the faster machine, and race rocket cars on it daily.
The salt around it is littered with failed gizmos and the craters they made. Cars have ended up as far away as Tanaris.
The gambling crowd is why both factions stand together at all.

cards.subject: The flats are contested
lines: Both factions quest out of the same racetrack, and the Shimmering Flats are a contested zone.
The safest-feeling place in Thousand Needles is the one where the other side is standing next to you.
